Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Setup: Some N-C vampire equips with a Writ of Acceptance [AH],
then does/gets a bunch of Cam-only stuff like:

1. Seizes Praxis (successfully)
2. Is named a Cam Exemplary
3. Is named an Archon

Then, some other minion steals/destroys the Writ, revoking our
hero's Camarilla status.

1. Is he still a Prince?
2. Is he still a Cam Exemplary?
3. Is he still an Archon?

Hairy question. My own feeling on this is that once such a Writ of Acceptance
is accepted, it is useful *only* as a reminder to the rest of the players that
this vampire has been accepted as a member of the Camarilla. Having never
actually come across this card in play, however, I haven't read it and thus
can't say for certain without reading what the card says.

First off, why is this different than something like Blood Bond, which
cannot target a Prince, but won't cease functioning if the target
eventually becomes a Prince?

----
Second, along the same lines, would a titled vamp still be a titled vamp if
he impersonates another clan?

1. Justicar (recognized as either the Justicar of the new or original clan)?
2. Prince (probably, since princes are city-based)?
3. Primogen?
4. Inner Circle member?

Would it make a difference if the impersonated clan was Non-Cam?

Likewise, if the Impersonator was named a Justicar of the impersonated
clan, and subsequently burned the Imperonation card, would he still
be a Justicar?

Impersonates a Camarilla clan?

If the votes/titles are lost, are they regianed once the vampire
ceases to impersonate. Or, if a title was gained while impersonating,
would the vampire regain the title if he re-impersonated the clan
after burning the first impersonation?

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
Daniel Hoffman <dhof...@cris.com> wrote:
>>> I see no reason why a vampire that stops being a Camarilla member would
>>> keep its Cam-only positions (e.g. Prince or Archon), but I'll have to
>>> double check on that.
>>If Bill Clinton emmigrates to Sweden, is he still the President??

I'm not a constitutional scholar, so I wouldn't know. But even if he isn't
automatically out, how long do you think it's going to be before Congress
impeaches him?

>If Bill Clinton's passport is stolen is he no longer a US citizen? The
>vampire isn't renouncing its camarilla status, it citizenship papers were
>stolen.

Why would the Camarilla possibly care why the vampire is no longer part of
their sect? A member of the Sabbat is a member of the Sabbat, whether she
went willingly, or got shanghaied with a shovel. It's highly unlikely that
a Writ of Acceptance (which I'm assuming your "passport" reference is to) is
carried around by a vampire, anyway. If a vampire is Accepted into the Cam,
the local Cam vampires will know this and treat them accordingly.

Certainly if a Prince defects to another sect, the Camarilla are going to
force him out of his seat and select a new Prince. The only real question is
whether it should be assumed in V:TES that the Cam knows it when
a member has left the sect.



Messages.Author: Zaphod Beeblebrox
Messages.Body:
mal...@macatawa.org wrote:

: On Wed, 12 Jun 1996, Daniel Hoffman wrote:

> I see no reason why a vampire that stops being a Camarilla member would
> keep its Cam-only positions (e.g. Prince or Archon), but I'll have to
> double check on that.

How is the ruling on being a Camarilla member phrased? I have
never seen an official statement on the concept. If the part
about being a prince reads something like "only Camarilla
vampires may be princes" then it seems a vampire who has his
status revoked would lose the title. However, if the rule is
that "only Camarilla vampires may call praxis seizure political
actions (and other Camarilla political actions, such as
Archon)" then the fact that your Ravnos, for instance, called
the PS as a Camarilla is the only condition necessary, and he
would retain the title. I'd like to see the active rule on
this issue, if anyone knows where I might find it.

-Dave Green

'like locquipment' != location.

I believe that he meant that once a vampire was equipped with this
particular piece of equipment, it should no longer be considered
equipment, _or anything else_. If cannot be stolen, traded, shattered,
arson'd, etc. It would act more like a non-unique title than a piece
of equipment.

Personally, I like the idea; It doesn't make sense that it can be
destroyed, stolen, _or_ traded to another vampire, personally.

Messages.Author: DOUGDWISE
Messages.Body:
I just imagine that this "Writ of Acceptance" Is like those mysterious
travel documents that allowed Victor Laszlo and Illsa Lund to leave
Casablanca (i.e., cannot be questioned and usable by whoever has them.)
The card test says that a Vampire who has the card is considered a member
of the Camarilla. Presumably then, one who no longer has it is not
considered a member and can no longer be Prince, Grand Poobah, or any
other Camarilla official. It would seem to make the card less confusing
to use.
Doug
